traits.smithy.api#documentation:
Bounded per AWS Batch Operations: a batch operation MUST have a documented
finite upper limit, and the limit counts entries so a caller can compute it
without serializing. 25 matches CampaignAssetTemplateList's own bound -- a kit
cannot hold more blueprints than one call can instantiate.

The asset template to instantiate, as returned by GetCampaignTemplate in
CampaignTemplate.AssetTemplates[].id.

Must belong to the campaign's own campaign template. An asset's editable
field schema is copied from this blueprint at creation and pinned, so an
asset without one could be neither validated on update nor made live.

Also this entry's request identifier: it MUST be unique across the
request's entries, since a campaign holds at most one asset per blueprint
(I-15) and two entries naming the same blueprint could not both succeed.

One blueprint to instantiate.

Carries nothing but the blueprint's identity, and that is the point rather
than a saving: category, name, FileFormat and platform are
all derived from the named blueprint, so no caller has a member with which to
contradict the pinned schema (asset design section 3.1).

There is deliberately no per-entry ClientToken. AWS Batch Operations requires a
*request identifier* per entry -- "a request identifier CAN either be a
resource identifier or a client idempotency token" -- and
SourceAssetTemplateIdentifier is a resource identifier, unique across entries
and echoed in this entry's error. Idempotency is structural rather than
token-based: an asset id is derived from (CampaignId, SourceAssetTemplateId),
so a replayed entry resolves to the same asset (I-16).

The failing entry's request identifier, so a caller can match this error
to the entry it sent.

Error code -- ResourceNotFoundException when the blueprint is not on the
campaign's bound template, InternalServerException otherwise. Throttling
never appears here: DG throttles per operation, so a throttle fails the
whole batch.

is no singular create. "Add the blueprint I skipped" is a batch of one.

One entry per blueprint that could not be instantiated. Empty, never
absent, when all entries succeeded.

One entry per asset that exists as a result of this call, whether created
here or already present.

Per-entry, per AWS Batch Operations. `Errors` is required and is empty rather
than absent on a fully successful call; `Successful` is the success list the
standard makes optional, and DG returns it because a client otherwise cannot
learn the ids that were created.

Status is 200 whenever entries were processed individually -- including when
every entry failed, since the batch itself succeeded and the entries did not.
A 4xx means the batch could not be attempted as a whole and nothing was
written.

A partial batch is a real state and the recovery is to re-send the same entry
list: an entry is idempotent by identity (I-15/I-16), so what landed no-ops
and what did not gets created. An already-existing asset is therefore a
`Successful` row, not an error -- were it an error, a client looping until
`Errors` is empty would never terminate.
The entry's request identifier.

The asset's identifier, derived from (CampaignId, SourceAssetTemplateId)

DOCUMENT only: the words a page uses for this document, such as "eBook". Fill an `AssetLink` field's
`LabelFieldId` with it when the partner picks this asset.

Whether the asset is live.

Reports current truth only, and nothing else on this shape overrides it. During an *initial*
publication it stays INACTIVE until the delivery platform holds the object; during a
*re*-publication it stays ACTIVE, because the previously published content is still serving.

A stopped asset and one never started both read INACTIVE; `LastActivationStatus` tells them
apart, because a stop does not change how the last activation went — stopped is INACTIVE with
that member `SUCCEEDED`, never started is INACTIVE with it absent.

An update never moves this member.

How the most recent hand-over to the delivery platform ended.

The hand-over, not the delivery: if DG got the artifact scheduled at the platform this is
SUCCEEDED, and whether the platform then delivered is `DeliveryStatus`. Per category the
hand-over point is — email: the mailing armed; social: the create, which *is* the schedule;
landing page: create plus publish-personalisation; document: bytes written.

Read with `State` this is what separates a stopped asset (INACTIVE with SUCCEEDED here) from
one never activated (INACTIVE with this member absent) — a stop does not change how the last
*activation* went.

There is no public UNKNOWN. A hand-over whose outcome DG cannot yet determine reports
IN_PROGRESS, because a partner's action is identical either way and there is nothing to do
with "unknown". Reporting it as FAILED would be the harmful collapse: that reads as safe to
retry, and a retry on an at-most-once create publishes a second live object.

Omitted before the first activation attempt.

What the platform did with the artifact after accepting it.

EMAIL and SOCIAL_POST only — absent on every other category, which has no delivery event.
See the DeliveryStatus docs.

Why delivery failed. Present only when DeliveryStatus is FAILED. For an email the platform
rejected: SENDER_EMAIL_INVALID, RECIPIENT_LIST_EMPTY, MAILING_CREDITS_EXHAUSTED or
RECIPIENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Otherwise DELIVERY_FAILED. A Facebook post refused because its
connection has no Page is FAILED with SOCIAL_CONNECTION_PAGE_REQUIRED, and withdrawn: reconnect
Facebook with a Page selected. A social post the platform stopped retrying, because it could not
publish within 12 hours of its scheduled time, is FAILED with DELIVERY_FAILED. Any other social post
that could not be published stays PENDING while it is investigated, and is reported FAILED with
DELIVERY_FAILED once it is confirmed it will not go out. Deactivate and activate the asset again to
retry.

The asset template this asset was created from: the `SourceAssetTemplateIdentifier` its

Set at create and never writable. Absent on an asset created before DG recorded it, which can't be
activated either. A campaign holds at most one asset per asset template, so this is how a
client matches a campaign's assets to its template's asset templates, for example to create the same
assets in another campaign. Names don't identify one: two asset templates can share a name.

value `CampaignAssetSummary.SocialPlatform` reports. Absent for every other category.

Concrete file format of the finished artifact. For `DOWNLOAD_ONLY` this is

When this asset sends, as chosen with UpdateCampaignAsset. `EMAIL` and `SOCIAL_POST` only — the two

The send time, present only when `SendMode` is `SCHEDULED`. It reaches the delivery platform at the

Was `scheduleDate: UtcDate`; retyped with the write member of the same name.

The asset's pinned template fields — the field schema copied from the
blueprint at instantiation, each paired with the partner's current value.
Present on every asset instantiated from a blueprint that offers editable
fields, whatever its category (design section 3.1); absent on one whose
blueprint offers none.

The asset's AWS-authored layout, as stable public CDN URLs composed from
the fileKeys copied off the blueprint at instantiation. Together with
FieldValues this makes the asset self-describing: a client renders the edit
form and shows the real layout while editing, with no template lookup.

The stored form is a bare object key and the URL is composed on read. The
key is revision-addressed and prior revisions are retained, so the key IS
the pin — nothing is copied into the asset bucket, and there is no version
parameter to carry (DG-038).

One entry for every category except LANDING_PAGE, which has two and
distinguishes them with PageType.

when none is stored); each option's own previews are on layout.options.

A multi-layout asset's layout choice (DG-044): the selection once made, and

FieldValues is always the union of every option's fields, selected or not,
so a client can switch layouts without a round trip: each option lists its

What must be fixed on this asset before it can be activated. Empty when the
asset is ready.

Issues don't block saving: an asset can be saved incomplete and fixed over
several updates. `StartCampaignAssetActivationTask` refuses an asset that
still has issues: an issue blocks activation when only an edit to the asset
can change the outcome. Most issues name the field to fix in `FieldId`. Fix it
with `UpdateCampaignAsset`, then read this list again.

Besides the issues computed from the asset's content, the list carries
what the last activation found: `CONTENT_REJECTED` and `PARTNER_IMAGE_REJECTED`
when moderation refused a field. Editing that field removes its issue. A
`CONTENT_REJECTED` without a `FieldId` means the text was refused as a whole;
editing any text field removes it.

with the partner's profile, such as a missing logo, are reported on

before anything has begun, so a narrower reading would be untrue. An asset

this is a **per-asset outcome
inside a task resource**. Identical values do not make two things the same

neither of its tasks fans out over independent children; this one does, so

Not live. Either never started, or started and since stopped — StartedAt
tells them apart. Also the position throughout an *initial* publication,
because nothing is live until the delivery platform holds the object.

Live: **the delivery platform holds the asset**, whether or not delivery
has since happened. A landing page is serving; a send or post is armed, or
has already gone out. Stays ACTIVE throughout a *re*-publication, because
the previously published content is still live while the new content is
handed over — and stays ACTIVE after delivery, because activation means the
platform is armed or serving and never meant anything had been delivered.
Delivery is reported separately by `DeliveryStatus`.

The lifecycle position of a campaign asset.

Answers exactly one question — is the asset live — and reports current truth
only. The evaluations *about* the asset are separate members:
`LastActivationStatus` for how the last hand-over to the delivery platform
ended, and `DeliveryStatus` for the send.
No member's value depends on another's, so there is nothing to rank.

`State` rather than `Status`, and narrowing this enum is what *earns* the
name rather than putting it at risk. The AWS Common Terms test for `State` is
whether a resource exposes "two or more resource attributes, one of which may
refer to status" — and `CampaignAsset` now exposes exactly that shape:
`State` beside `LastActivationStatus` and `DeliveryStatus`. So this is no longer a lone enum dressed up as a condition;
it is the lifecycle position sitting next to the named status attributes,
flat rather than nested. Read on its own the member looks like a single
attribute and the standard would ask for `Status`; read on the resource it is
the aggregate the standard reserves `State` for. Same-domain precedent:
Amazon Connect Campaigns uses `State` for a campaign's lifecycle and
`Status` for a job. Recorded for API office hours.

Distinguish a stopped asset from one never started by whether StartedAt is
set; StartedAt is never cleared, not even by a stop.

This enum carried five values, `IN_PROGRESS` and `FAILED` alongside the two
below plus `COMPLETED`, and all three were removed rather than deprecated.

`IN_PROGRESS` and `FAILED` went because **a single projected value could not
answer "is it live?"** — a live asset with a scan in flight and a *stopped*
asset with a scan in flight both projected `IN_PROGRESS`, and `FAILED`
collapsed the same way, because the projection ranked its inputs by a frozen
precedence and precedence discards facts. The fact it discarded was liveness.
The three internal axes the projection read now map onto this member plus
`LastActivationStatus` plus one internal-only distinction, with no information
lost. See campaign-asset-design.md §2 and §6.

`COMPLETED` went because it was doing delivery's job: it meant "delivered",
which is a delivery outcome and not a lifecycle position. For an email it was
exactly `DeliveryStatus = DELIVERED`, already modelled and already on the
asset; for a social post it was **unachievable**, because this service cannot
observe social delivery at all — so half of its stated meaning, "the email was
sent, or the post published", was never reachable. The other three startable
types have no delivery event whatever. It had no writer and no reader.

Anyone reintroducing a terminal position needs a fact observable for **every**
startable type, which `DeliveryStatus` explicitly is not — it covers only EMAIL
and SOCIAL_POST.

An open set of `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` tokens, deliberately typed as a string
rather than an enum. `ConflictException` is shared by every resource in this
service, so an enum here would accumulate values that are meaningful for one
resource and inapplicable to the rest — the cohesiveness problem the Backward

would force an SDK regeneration on callers who can never encounter it.
Clients MUST treat an unrecognised value as an unspecified conflict and fall

Values in use today:

From the campaign asset activation path. Every one of these is decided before the
operation returns, so a caller that receives one knows nothing was started.

These two are thrown by `DeactivateCampaignAsset`, which refuses one asset
outright. `StartCampaignAssetActivationTask` reports the same two causes
**per asset** as a FAILED task entry instead of throwing, because one bad
identifier must not refuse the twenty-four good ones beside it — so the
spellings are deliberately identical to `CampaignAssetStateReason`'s,
letting a client match one string whichever way the refusal arrived. The two
types evolve independently on purpose: this is an open string shared by every
resource, that is a closed enum owned by one operation.

- `ASSET_START_IN_PROGRESS` — the asset is already being started, or another
  caller changed it during this request. Retryable once the outcome is visible.
- `PREREQUISITE_ASSET_NOT_ACTIVE` — this asset embeds output from another asset
  that is not live. `ResourceId` carries that asset's identifier.

From the prerequisite edges between a campaign's assets — an email that embeds its landing page's URL.
Both refuse the whole request and write nothing.

- `PREREQUISITE_ASSET_MISSING` — from `BatchCreateCampaignAsset`: an entry's blueprint embeds another
  blueprint's output, and that blueprint is neither named in the same request nor already an asset
  on the campaign. Retry with it in the request. `ResourceId` carries the missing blueprint's
  identifier.
- `ASSET_HAS_DEPENDENTS` — from `DeleteCampaignAsset`: another asset on the campaign embeds this
  asset's output, so deleting it would leave that asset unactivatable. Delete the dependents first.
  The message names them.

`CAMPAIGN_COMPLETED` — the campaign is complete (the UTC date is after its `EndOn`), so it and its assets
are read-only. Refuses `UpdateCampaign`, `BatchCreateCampaignAsset`, `UpdateCampaignAsset`,
`DeleteCampaignAsset` and `StartCampaignAssetActivationTask`; never `DeactivateCampaignAsset`. **Not
retryable, and not fixable** — `EndOn` cannot be moved once it has passed, so nothing the caller does
will make the write succeed. `ResourceId` carries the campaign identifier.

⚠️ This is the one conflict reason whose condition **never clears**, which sits awkwardly with
`ConflictException` promising a state that may change. It is a conflict rather than a validation
failure because the request is well formed and would have succeeded a moment earlier — the resource's
state is what refuses it, which is what this exception is for. Contrast `ASSET_NOT_STARTABLE`, which
moved to `ValidationException` precisely because it is a property of the asset's *type* rather than
of its state.

⚠️ **`COMPLETED` also exists as a `CampaignAssetExportTaskStatus` value, on a different axis.** That
one means an export archive finished assembling. The two are unrelated and must not be unified.

`CAMPAIGN_HAS_ACTIVE_ASSETS` — from `DeleteCampaign`: at least one of the campaign's assets is live,
and deleting the campaign would orphan what the delivery platform still serves or sends. Deactivate
those assets with `DeactivateCampaignAsset`, then retry. The message names them. `ResourceId`
carries the campaign identifier.

`CAMPAIGN_ACTIVATION_IN_PROGRESS` — from
`StartCampaignAssetActivationTask` and `DeleteCampaign`, refusing the whole request: one activation
task runs on a campaign at a time. `ResourceId` carries the **holding task's
id**, so a caller can poll `GetCampaignAssetActivationTask` rather than guess.
Retryable once that task reaches a terminal status.

`SERVICE_LINKED_ROLE_DELETION_IN_PROGRESS` — from `StartCampaignAssetActivationTask`, refusing the
whole request: this service's service-linked role is being deleted, so no asset may go live. Not a
lease conflict: `ResourceId` is unset and there is no task to poll. Retryable after a short wait; if
the role was deleted, the next activation recreates it.

`LAYOUT_LOCKED_AFTER_ACTIVATION` — from `UpdateCampaignAsset`, refusing a `Layout`
change on a multi-layout asset that has activated successfully at least once
(DG-044). The published object is that layout's, so switching would leave the
asset describing a layout that is not the one live. **Not fixable**: the asset
keeps its layout for life. A failed activation does not lock it. Re-sending the
layout already selected is not a change and is accepted. `ResourceId` carries
the asset identifier.

`ASSET_START_IN_PROGRESS` — also from `UpdateCampaignAsset`, refusing any edit to
an asset the campaign's running activation task has accepted and not yet finished:
the run publishes the content it read, so an edit accepted mid-run would either be
published unvalidated or never published. Nothing is written. Retryable once the
asset's outcome on the task (`GetCampaignAssetActivationTask`) is terminal; the
asset's siblings may still be running. `ResourceId` carries the asset identifier.

`ASSET_ALREADY_ACTIVE` — from `UpdateCampaignAsset`, refusing any change to a live
email or social post, content or schedule. Deactivate it first; the next
activation sends everything current. Landing pages and documents are edited
live and converge by re-activation. `ResourceId` carries the asset identifier.

`ASSET_NOT_DEACTIVATABLE` — from `DeactivateCampaignAsset`, for an asset that
can't be stopped: a document, banner or landing page until the campaign has
completed, when it becomes removable. Until then, update it and activate it
again. `ResourceId` carries the asset identifier.

`ASSET_HAS_LOCKED_SENDS` — from `DeactivateCampaignAsset`, within an hour of the
asset's send (a social post's publish), when it can no longer be withdrawn.
`ASSET_ALREADY_DELIVERED` — the same, once that time has passed: a sent email or
a published post cannot be recalled. Neither is retryable.

Three values were removed with the campaign lifecycle and the singular
activate, and none should be re-added here:

- `CAMPAIGN_NOT_STARTED` — a campaign has no state to be started out of.
- `ASSET_NOT_STARTABLE` — moved to `ValidationException`, with no reason. The
  value's own documentation said it was "not retryable and not fixable: it is a
  property of the asset's type", and `ConflictException` promises a state that
  may change. The gate itself stays — deleting it lets a download-only asset
  into a task with no dispatch arm, which would succeed and do nothing.
- `ASSET_START_UNCONFIRMED` — described a state that no longer occurs. DG cannot
  be more idempotent than a platform whose social create has no idempotency
  key, so an ambiguous hand-over is now an ordinary failure carrying

Takes a **list** because the service owns the ordering. Assets link to one
another by URL — an email's call-to-action carries the landing page's URL, the
landing page's download field carries the document's — and a URL does not
exist until the asset it points at is activated. Those edges are derived by

topologically sorting them is work the service has already done, and getting
it wrong arms an email with a dead link. Name every asset you want live and
the service sequences them; "activate everything" is the list with every id
in it, which ListCampaignAssets already gave you.

platform. Everything decidable **without** a write to the delivery platform is

applies to the whole request — a malformed list, an unknown campaign, another

overlapping runs made the per-asset status misleading rather than merely
contended.
